Inspiring Inquiring Minds
Our Vision
At Pembury House we believe that high quality nursery education can transform the lives of young children and that partnership with parents provides the basis for successful learning. We work as a team to ensure that children:
Are valued as individuals.
Feel happy, confident and safe in the nursery school and children’s centre.
Feel included and listen and learn from each other.
Develop confidence, independence and a positive view of themselves.
Learn through play and first-hand experiences.
Acquire the knowledge, skills and attitude they need, now and in the future, in a rapidly changing world.

British Values
Pembury House Nursery School and Children’s Centre actively promotes the fundamental values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths or beliefs.
These are interpreted by our children as learning right from wrong; learning to take turns and share; and challenging negative views and stereotypes. We do not promote views and theories that are contrary to established scientific or historical evidence and explanations.
Pembury House Nursery School and Children’s Centre actively promotes these fundamental British Values:
What do children learn at Pembury?
We respect everybody as individuals, celebrate difference in people and support children to take turns and share
At Pembury we are learning right from wrong. We work together to agree rules. We are learning to share and take turns. We all help to tidy up.
We listen to everyone’s point of view. Children are helped to make the right choices and are encouraged to become independent.
We share learning between home and school and encourage parents to be actively involved in their children’s learning. We value children as individuals and respect all cultures, beliefs and languages.
We encourage positive behaviour and attitudes towards others. We enjoy the rich cultural and ethnic mix of Pembury families and celebrate diversity.

pageCache.text:
Inspiring Inquiring Minds
HEADTEACHER’S WELCOME
Inspiring Inquiring Minds
At Pembury House children and families sit at the heart of everything that we do.
It is important to us that we work together in partnership with parents and carers, to share children’s interests and learning, and to help them be the best they can be.
Children learn best through play, first-hand experiences and meaningful conversations. At Pembury we aim to inspire children to become independent curious learners and support them to become confident communicators. Our exciting and creative curriculum provides challenging opportunities to explore and learn. Children enjoy a variety of research and creative projects. We have a wonderful garden for children to play and learn through nature. Providing an inclusive education for all underpins the values we hold at Pembury House.
We have fantastic on-site children’s centre facilities offering a range of health, education and advice sessions for families with children under 5. These include our popular parent and toddler ‘Stay and Play’ sessions and Baby Groups.
I am privileged to lead a fantastic team where everyone has the children’s best interests at heart and provide a fantastic, creative and exciting education for our children.
We are so proud of our school and children’s centre - Come and take a look !
Here you will find nursery education, as well as full day care provision, for children and children centre services available in our well- resourced and purpose built building.
I look forward to meeting you!

Early Years Pupil Premium 2025
Early Years Pupil Premium
Since April 2015, early years pupil premium (EYPP) is additional funding for early years settings to improve the education they provide for disadvantaged 3- and 4-year-olds. Children must receive free early education in order to attract EYPP funding.
The funding builds on the school-age pupil premium, introduced in schools in 2011. Nationally, the statistics show that disadvantaged children often do less well than their peers at school. The aim of this money is to try to close the attainment gap between pupils and to try to remove any barriers to learning that pupils may face. Children who meet the criteria will be eligible for an extra 53p per hour.
3- and 4-year-olds in state-funded early education will attract EYPP funding if they meet at least 1 of the following criteria: - their family gets 1 of the following:
- they are currently being looked after by a local authority in England or Wales
- they have left care in England or Wales through:

pageCache.pageTitle: Pembury House Nursery - Services and Partnerships
pageCache.text:
Services and Partnerships
Pembury House Children’s Centre offers a wide range of services for children under 5 and their parents from the local community.
One You Haringey - 12 week physical activity course
Please click here for more information regarding the One you Haringey FREE 12 week physical activity course.
Antenatal/Postnatal appointments
This is an invite-only service provided by midwives from both North Middlesex and Whittington Hospitals. We also host the MAIA team delivering Better Births.
Better Births, the national review of maternity services launched in 2016 is piloting models of care, with the objective to achieve continuity of care/carer, and personalising care and working across boundaries along with other aims.
If you would like to know more about Better Births, take a look at the National Maternity Review report which outlines a five year forward view for maternity care. This document will increasingly influence the way forward in maternity.
Health Visitor Team development checks
They are invite-only appointments where families join the Community Nursery Nurse from the Health Visiting Team to discuss their child’s developmental progress.
Silva, one of our EIOPs, regularly visits the Baby Clinic at Tynemouth Road, where you can weigh your baby every Wednesday form 10am-12pm. If you would like to know more about the services offered for you and your child by Tynemouth Medical Practice, you can do so here.
Baby Group
For new parents, we have our friendly and supportive baby group. Come along and meet other new parents and babies! This is for all babies (under 1 year old) in the area and their families: you and your child can play together, make new friends, speak to staff and access other services such as breastfeeding, introducing solid feeding, supporting your child’s sleeping, baby massage, etc.
We sometimes invite special guests – these include our Link Health Visitor (to talk about immunisations, sleeping patterns and feeding) and the Oral Health Practitioner. This service is free of charge.
Please see current timetable for more information regarding group timings
Stay and Play Groups
For children aged up to 5 years old and their parents/carers, we run stay and play groups twice a week. These offer a range of exciting opportunities for learning through play. Come and join us for messy play, water play, singing and reading, and exploring outdoors! This service is free of charge.
These sessions are also a good opportunity for you and your child to enjoy playtime together, make new friends, speak to our friendly team and access other services such as speech and language, support to access nursery, behaviour tips and advice, housing and many more.
Please see current timetable for more information regarding group timings
Chattertots
Invitation only! For families with children from 18 months to 3 years old. Chattertots is a language and communication focused group that supports parents and children through songs, rhymes and stories. You are also welcome to have a chat with our staff after the session if you have any questions or would need more personalised support.
Please ask Sylvie or Tameeka for more information. This service is free of charge.
Adult Learning
Are you interested in working in Early Years Education and Childcare? We offer a range of Early Years CACHE accredited courses at Levels 1, 2 and 3. These are run by Barnet and Southgate College. Please ask our office or Children's Centre team for more information.
Would you like to improve your English? Find out about our ESOL classes, run by WEA. We have a range of courses at different levels.
Please ask Simone at Reception for more information.

A Message from our Chair of Governors
Together we represent a broad spectrum of occupations and bring invaluable community experience and expertise to the leadership of Pembury House Nursery School & Children’s Centre.
The Governors of Pembury House Nursery School & Children’s Centre are rightly proud of the school and the high quality of education that it offers to the community. Each governor is assigned to a committee and makes visits as part of a monitoring and evaluation process. The School Development Plan is reviewed regularly and targets set to ensure that our priorities are clear.
As Chair of Governors I am very aware that, in order to achieve the highest standards for our pupils, we must always strive for excellence, and by working closely with the school, community and parents we aim to continue our success.

Music Specialist
Music, Movement, Songs and Rhymes are really important and valued at Pembury House.
Music making in early years is crucial to support language, maths, motor skills and emotional growth through activities like singing, dancing and playing instruments.
At Pembury House we integrate music and movement naturally into routines and activities to built foundations for literacy and numeracy through rhythm, patterns and repetition, while developing coordination and creativity through movement and exploration.
Singing, dancing and playing instruments foster self-expression, confidence, connection and well-being.
